summary: Feed 'encrypted_share' to IDS is degraded: 82.0% encrypted bytes exceeds IDS tolerance of 60%, limiting payload inspection. All other visibility checks (duplicates, VLANs, one-way, drops, overload) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: 82% of bytes are encrypted (metric 0.8198 vs threshold 0.6), likely due to predominantly TLS/HTTPS traffic being forwarded to the IDS without prior decryption or selective bypass on the packet broker.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload inspection and tolerates ~60% encrypted traffic; at 82% the payload is opaque, causing missed signatures, reduced detection coverage, and blind spots for threats inside encrypted sessions.

recommended_fix.why: Deploy SSL/TLS visibility/decryption for relevant traffic or selectively filter/bypass trusted encrypted flows at the packet broker to bring encrypted share below 60% and restore IDS payload inspection capability.
